To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Grad CAM and Guiding Grad CAM can be used to visualize and explain predictions from deep networks, (2) these visualizations are useful for better understanding the behavior of deep networks, (3) they are broadly applicable to any deep network architecture, (4) they are useful for better explaining predictions made by image captioning and visual question answering models, and (5) they are useful in the context of human computer interaction for helping users establish trust in deep networks.

(a) we introduce a technique for visualizing the discriminative regions in images using deep networks that requires no re training; (b) our technique can be used to visualize discriminative regions in a variety of image classification, image annotation and visual question answering applications; and (c) our visualizations can be used to help untrained users establish trust in predictions made by deep neural networks.

Grad CAM visual explanations can be used to (a) gain a deeper understanding of how deep neural network models make predictions and (b) help users establish trust with the predictions made by these models.
